what_its_for: Roflumilast is used to reduce the number of flare-ups (called exacerbations) in adults with severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It helps decrease swelling and irritation in the lungs. It is NOT a rescue inhaler and will NOT treat a sudden breathing attack.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Do not crush or split the tablet. If you have stomach upset, try taking it with a small snack or meal.
dosing: The usual dose is one 500 mcg (microgram) tablet once a day. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose of 250 mcg once daily for the first 4 weeks to help reduce side effects, then increase to 500 mcg. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next regular dose as scheduled. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medications safely out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking, as it worsens COPD. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially antibiotics like rifampin, seizure medicines, or antifungal drugs, because they can affect how roflumilast works in your body. Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it may increase the risk of side effects. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: new or worsening feelings of sadness, depression, anxiety, or thoughts of harming yourself or suicide; significant unexplained weight loss; severe diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain that does not go away; headache that is severe or unusual; sleep problems; dizziness or feeling faint; or any allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Seek emergency help immediately if you have thoughts of suicide.
when_it_works: Roflumilast does not work right away. It may take several weeks to months before you notice fewer COPD flare-ups. Keep taking it every day even if you feel fine. Do not stop without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as safety has not been fully established. Liver problems: Do NOT take roflumilast if you have moderate to severe liver disease. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in anyone under 18 years old. Older adults: No special dose adjustment is needed for age alone, but report any unusual side effects to your doctor promptly.
